Karen's search for a roommate leads to a high-maintenance individual, who shares many of her eccentricities; Grace and Jack intervene when Will uses painkillers as a crutch.
Karen hires a somewhat immature divorce attorney (guest star Macaulay Culkin) to oppose Will in court.
When Karen's ex-husband dies, she and her British rival (Minnie Driver) have a contest of wills; Leo (Harry Connick Jr.) is needed in Guatemala.
Karen confronts her ex-husband's mistress before inviting everybody for a ceremony on her yacht; Grace suffers from jealousy after meeting her husband's sexy co-worker.
Will and Jack awake in a precarious position while at sea; Grace discovers love letters in Leo's bag from a female colleague.
Grace is vexed when she learns that Leo's ex-girlfriend (Mira Sorvino) is intimately acquainted with Will.
Karen invites Grace and Leo to play tennis at her exclusive club, but her fierce playing style drives Grace away.
Jack lands a speaking role opposite James Earl Jones in an off-Broadway play and gives the veteran actor some pointers.
Will takes Leo on shopping sprees and for high tea to help him rekindle his love of the city; Karen coaches Jack for the annual gay spelling bee.
Will takes his mother for an afternoon stroll and bumps into an attractive bachelor (Dylan McDermott); Karen continues her lifelong quest to hunt down hubby-stealing Lorraine.
An unorthodox doctor (Jack Black) gives Karen her annual physical; Jack begs Will to support his decision to become a student nurse.
Will urges Grace to stay in New York so they can spend some time together; Karen strong-arms Jack's nursing teacher into letting him skip class but still make the grade.
Will catches the eye of a female diner after being stood up; Grace bumps into a man (Tom Everett Scott) with whom she once shared a forgettable encounter; Karen runs into her nemesis, Candice Bergen.

A weak bladder forces Will to entrust Grace with his place in line for Barry Manilow tickets; Grace's mother (Debbie Reynolds) cancels their annual mother-daughter shopping trip to have dinner with Jack.

Grace's freeloading sister (Geena Davis) comes to town to launch her latest business enterprise; Karen spurns Lyle (John Cleese), then changes her mind after Lorraine (Minnie Driver) expresses her disapproval.
A rich plastic surgeon (guest star Hal Linden) tries to buy Will's affection; Grace boycotts a new restaurant.
Will's new client (Dave Foley) falls for Jack; Grace and Karen discover hidden money while trying to fix the plumbing in Leo's cabin.
Will is the only single man in a cooking class full of couples, including Jack and his new boyfriend (Dave Foley); Karen's mother (Suzanne Pleshette) asks Grace to decorate her apartment.
Will and Grace begin a business venture selling apartments; Jack runs into his former acting mentor, Zandra; Karen and Lyle (John Cleese) try to renew romance.
Will and Grace try to break up Jack and Stuart (Dave Foley) so they can sell the apartment for a higher price; Karen demands that Lyle (John Cleese) discipline his daughter (Minnie Driver).
Real estate entrepreneurs Will and Grace face formidable competition on the East Side from a lesbian couple (Edie Falco, Chloë Sevigny); John Edward gives Karen some psychic guidance.
Jack and Grace stumble upon Stuart (Dave Foley) watching a movie matinée in the company of another man; Will tries to teach Karen how to drive.
Grace advises Will to play hard to get with his new boyfriend (Bobby Cannavale); Jack and Karen despair after learning their favorite TV series will be going off the air.
Will introduces his new boyfriend (Bobby Cannavale) to overly critical Grace; Karen tells Jack that their friendship will change after her wedding.
At Tina's (Lesley Ann Warren) urging, Will tries to find out if there is a new woman in his father's life; Jack's son decides to try out for the high-school cheerleading squad.
On the eve of his graduation from nursing school, Jack turns to Will for help writing his commencement address.
Karen moves her wedding to Las Vegas, where Jennifer Lopez agrees to sing at the ceremony.
Karen recruits Jack to help her get Jennifer Lopez to listen to Karen's new song; Grace takes out her frustration over her cheating husband on Will.
Jack wangles his way into Janet Jackson's (guest starring as herself) performance tour as a backup dancer.
As she attempts to steal doughnuts at an AA meeting, Grace has a surprise reunion with Val (Molly Shannon); Will and Jack attend a gay television focus group meeting.
Grace accuses Will of being too nice to strangers; Jack has trouble at his new company when his co-workers mock him about his Cher doll.
Despite the fact that Will has never had a happy birthday, his new relationship with Vince (Bobby Cannavale) gives him hope that this one will be.
Will convinces Jack to aid a local gay-bookstore owner to save his store from closing.
Will and Grace decide to invite Vince and Nadine (Kristin Davis) over, but they quickly learn that, despite similarities in friendship, they are polar opposites.
After a great date with someone else, Grace comes home to a garbled message from Leo; Karen and Jack try to set each other up, but things go awry.
Will, Grace, Jack and Karen go on a road trip for Grace's getaway weekend, but Jack and Karen hate the car ride and bail on the plan.

Vince's mother cannot make her traditional holiday feast, so Will volunteers to make a special meal, but Vince's mother refuses to give him any credit; Jack gives Vince's sister (Jamie-Lynn DiScala) pointers on keeping secrets.
Will makes the holiday meal.
Grace accidentally breaks a treasured figurine at Will's mother's (Blythe Danner) holiday party and blames it on another guest.
An old classmate (Jeff Goldblum) tries to get revenge on Karen by becoming the president of Walker Inc.; Will and Grace run into Vince and a co-worker while playing hooky from work.
Will is reluctant to bring Vince to a dinner party at his boss's (Lily Tomlin) home, fearing it will scratch his chances of making partner at the firm.
When Scott Woolley (Jeff Goldblum) tries to get Grace to fire Karen by impersonating a restaurant owner, the women plan a trap for him.

Although Grace tries to ignore St. Valentine's Day, she winds up with a hunky greeting-card writer (Ed Burns); Karen's former nemesis (Jeff Goldblum) tries to win her heart by showering her with gifts.

Grace drags Will along on her first date with Nick (Edward Burns); Karen tries to set Jack up on a date with the neighborhood bird enthusiast (Luke Perry), but things don't quite go as she has planned.
When Will agrees to fire Karen's pastry chef, he becomes involved in a love triangle that the baker created.
When Jack convinces Will that they need a change of scenery, they buy an apartment in an up-and-coming gay community.
Will is jealous when his no-nonsense therapist (guest star Sharon Stone) becomes fast friends with Grace.
Grace convinces Karen to attend her father's (Alan Arkin) birthday party; Karen entertains herself by spending time with Martin's friend Burt (Lee Majors).
Grace's near-death experience prompts her to write her will and jolts Will into making a life-altering career choice.
When Will's writing career fizzles, Malcolm (Alec Baldwin) makes him another job offer; Grace's old college flame (Eric Stoltz) gives her a job decorating his new hotel.
Will becomes suspicious of his new job when he finds himself in an empty office with a German shepherd and a Russian-speaking thug.
Grace contemplates an affair with a married man (Eric Stoltz); Jack begins his new career as a talk-show host; Will continues to hide from Karen the fact that Stan is alive.
When Will suspects that Karen is more upset about Stan being alive than she is letting on, he makes it his mission to help her heal emotionally.
Jack learns that Will has never learned how to swim, so he makes it his mission to teach him.
Jack tells Karen he believes she belongs with Stan, not Malcolm (Alec Baldwin).
Jack brings Baby Glenn (Jason Biggs), who gained notoriety in the '80s after being trapped in a hole for days, to Will's charity auction and carnival.
Grace and Will spot her ex-husband, Leo, on their plane to London; Will charms a pair of gay flight attendants into letting Grace into first-class to talk with Leo.
Jack's decision to move makes Will take a close look at their friendship; Karen and Grace are invited to the memorial celebration for Beverly's (Leslie Jordan) deceased wife.
When Grace finds it impossible to please her mother, Jack offers to help, believing no one knows how to be a good daughter like a gay son.
When the gang spends Christmas at the home of Will's mother, Marilyn Truman (Blythe Danner), Grace gets romantic with Will's brother.
"The Sound of Music Sing-Along" has come to town and no one is more excited than Grace; she plans for her and Will to attend the musical in character-like style by dressing up in costumes.
All of New York society attend Karen's birthday party, but Will, Grace and Jack embarrass themselves and get stuck in the bathroom with the birthday girl.
Will insists that Grace turn down a job offer from his former boss, Margot, who has asked Grace to redecorate the law firm.
Will and Grace dread a dinner date with Rob and Ellen, but the identity of their waiter (Bobby Cannavale) eclipses their friends' big news.
Will, Karen and Grace travel to Los Angeles to support Jack as he accepts an award for Best Local Cable Guy Talk Show Host.
Karen ignores Grace's plea for a low-key wedding and plans a huge affair, hiring Hall & Oates to perform "Maneater" at the ceremony.
Nervous but optimistic Grace decides it is time to tell Leo (Harry Connick Jr.) she is pregnant with his child.
Ecstatic, Jack coerces Will into coming out with him to a cowboy bar to meet his new boyfriend, Travis.
A large corporation takes over OutTV, completely revamping Jack's talk show and giving him a conservative co-host, Britney Spears.
Jack loses his hosting job and vows never to return to acting; Will has a showdown with his father.
At his father's funeral, Will grapples with their last encounter; Grace begins to doubt her potential to be a good mother.
Will and Grace attend childbirth classes; Karen seeks comfort from very busy Jack.
Vince's plans to move into a brownstone with Will do not include Grace; Jack's show premieres.
Will and Grace make a decision about their future together; Jack continues his never-ending search for love; Karen tries to find happiness in Stan's absence.
Valentine's Day finds the gang at the Max reminiscing about past relationships. With Mark-Paul Gosselaar and Dustin Diamond.
Zack's plan to encourage the teachers to strike backfires on the students when the Academic Bowl is canceled.
The gang scrambles for dates as the senior prom approaches. With Mark-Paul Gosselaar and Mario Lopez.
A look into the future finds Belding with six students who are very similar to the gang from the class of 1993.
Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) is desperate enough to try ballet class when he learns he needs one more credit to graduate.
Zack's partner for a school project is the new girl at Bayside, a tough biker who is not at all impressed with him.
Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) becomes overprotective of the physically challenged girl he is counseling on the teen line.
Zack and Slater (Mark-Paul Gosselaar, Mario Lopez) bet to see who can kiss Tori (Leanna Creel) first.
Zack tries to sneak out of detention so he can participate in a contest that has a trip to Hawaii as the prize.
Slater, Lisa, Zack and Screech (Mario Lopez, Lark Voorhies, Mark-Paul Gosselaar, Dustin Diamond) are involved in a drunken driving accident.
Zack talks everyone into buying class rings from a man named Gem Diamond.
The guys and the girls stage a competition to decide who gets to spend a $10,000 inheritance. With Lark Voorhies and Dustin Diamond.
Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) dates Slater's sister despite his friend's nervousness about the matter. With Mario Lopez.
Mrs. Belding (guest star Louan Gideon) goes into labor while trapped in an elevator with Zack and Tori (Mark-Paul Gosselaar, Leanna Creel).
Zack, Slater, Screech and Lisa (Mark-Paul Gosselaar, Mario Lopez, Dustin Diamond, Lark Voorhies) reflect on the summer they spent at Malibu Sands.
Zack enters a contest to write a new school song and resorts to sabotage.
Zack's summer romance with an older woman comes to a halt when she discovers he lied to her.
Zack promises to help Screech get a date with Lisa if Screech will do Zack's term paper.
Zack tries to cash in on a stock-market investment to get money to replace his father's video recorder.
A student opposed to killing animals for experiments releases all the science class frogs.
Zack's father falls for Miss Bliss.
Screech finds that an intimidating student has a learning disability.
Zack and a classmate ask the same girl to an upcoming dance, jeopardizing their friendship.
Zack's (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) scheme to get more time to study for a midterm ends up hurting his teacher. With Dennis Haskins.
A student argument helps a teacher resolve a problem with a longtime friend. With Mark-Paul Gosselaar and Dustin Diamond.
A teacher turns a practical joke into a lesson about the criminal justice system. With Mark-Paul Gosselaar and Dustin Diamond.
Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) schemes to steal a kiss from a returning former student who is now a famous rock star.
Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) is offered a chance to join a popular club. With Dustin Diamond.
A retired teacher with unorthodox methods stimulates the class when he substitutes for their regular teacher.
The gang enters a dance contest being held at the Max and hosted by radio personality Casey Kasem. With Mark-Paul Gosselaar and Dustin Diamond.
Lisa's (Lark Voorhies) friends invent ways to pay the bills she has accrued on her father's credit card. With Tiffani-Amber Thiessen and Mark-Paul Gosselaar.
A freak lightning accident enables Screech (Dustin Diamond) to predict the future. With Tiffani-Amber Thiessen and Mario Lopez.
The guys hide a microphone at the girls' party to find out whom Kelly will ask to the dance.
Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) gets into unusual circumstances and clothes when he tries to help Screech (Dustin Diamond) get a date.
Zack's (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) plan to get rid of Slater (Mario Lopez) backfires; Slater's revenge ends up benefiting Screech (Dustin Diamond).
When Ms. Simpson injures her back, a substitute teacher named Tony Crane takes over her class at Bayside; when all the girls fall for Mr. Crane, Zack and Slater become jealous.
When Kelly is nominated as homecoming queen, her dream is shattered as she faces the prospect of winning after she gets a zit; Zack comes up with a solution, but it does not unfold as he plans.
Zack bets against a Valley wrestler named Marvin Nedick that Slater will win his wrestling match against Nedick; things go wrong when Slater decides to quit wrestling.
In order for Kelly to go to a George Michael concert, she has to pass her science test. Zack persuades Screech to tutor Kelly, a ploy which is more for his benefit than for Kelly's.
Zack and his friends form a company selling friendship bracelets for a business class project. He names himself as boss, but Kelly, Jessie, and Slater feel he is treating them poorly.
Everyone is put into pairs for a class assignment to act out married life, so they can be prepared for marriage as adults.
Jessie and Zack (Elizabeth Berkley, Mark-Paul Gosselaar) run for student president, each for different reasons.
Zack's use of a subliminal tape to get Kelly to fall for him has results he never intended.
Zack's (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) schemes to get Kelly (Tiffani-Amber Thiessen) to be his girl land him in detention with a rival for her affections.
The pranks between rival schools Bayside and Valley escalate during the week of the city cheerleading finals.
Screech's (Dustin Diamond) alien disguise is so believable it attracts a government UFO investigator.
Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) decides to throw a surprise birthday party for Screech (Dustin Diamond) in the principal's office.
Slater's (Mario Lopez) pet dies while in Zack's (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) care.
Kelly (Tiffani-Amber Thiessen) chooses to go to the prom with Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar); Lisa and Screech (Lark Voorhies, Dustin Diamond) have a "trial" date.
Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) becomes a leader of men when he joins a cadet corps to get out of detention.
The gang uses an old radio station in the school basement to hold a marathon. With Mark-Paul Gosselaar and Dustin Diamond.
Zack's antics get Slater thrown out of driver education classes.
Screech's (Dustin Diamond) house party turns into a disaster when his mother's favorite statue is broken. With Mark-Paul Gosselaar.
Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) tries to cope when he ends up with two dates for the same night; Jessie (Elizabeth Berkley) agrees to a blind date.
Zack has a waiter impersonate his father for a meeting with the principal.
The Miss Bayside Beauty Pageant attracts unusual contestants; Zack and Slater (Mark-Paul Gosselaar, Mario Lopez) make a bet.
Jessie (Elizabeth Berkley) becomes addicted to caffeine pills as she strives to be a perfect student. With Mark-Paul Gosselaar, Tiffani-Amber Thiessen.
Zack's (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) "Girls of Bayside" calendar catches the eye of a fashion photographer. With Dustin Diamond.
Zack's (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) advice line backfires and gets him into trouble with everyone. With Mario Lopez.

Zack makes a surprising discovery about his Native American heritage; Lisa learns her family tree includes a Black American hero of the Underground Railroad; Jessie grapples with guilt over her slave-trading ancestry.
Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) asks Kelly (Tiffani-Amber Thiessen) to go steady and then falls in love with the school nurse.
Mr. Belding's brother Rod (guest star Edward Blatchford) scores points with the class as a substitute history teacher. With Dennis Haskins and Mark-Paul Gosselaar.
Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) plots to reunite Slater (Mario Lopez), Mr. Belding (Dennis Haskins) and himself with their feuding sweethearts.
Some underhanded shenanigans are employed to win a glee club competition.
A costume ball sets the stage for Zack and Kelly (Mark-Paul Gosselaar, Tiffani-Amber Thiessen) to examine their relationship.
Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) has a hard time dealing with the fact that Kelly (Tiffani-Amber Thiessen) has a new boyfriend.
A minor accident sends Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) to the hospital, where he nervously faces the prospect of surgery.
Panic hits when Screech (Dustin Diamond) finds out he has to play a Russian exchange student in the chess finals. With Dennis Haskins.
Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) tries to impress a college girl by lying about his age.
The students adopt a new mascot when a stray ball injures a duck in the pond behind the football field.
Jessie's stepbrother Eric arrives from New York and blackmails her, Zack and Slater (Elizabeth Berkley, Mark-Paul Gosselaar, Mario Lopez).
Eric tries to blackmail Slater (Mario Lopez) and learns a disturbing truth about his date with Lisa (Lark Voorhies).
The student council decides to hold a dance-date auction to raise money for new cheerleading uniforms.
Richard takes the Volkswagen Touareg 4x4 to Sweden; Tom Cruise and Cameron Diaz are the "Stars in a Reasonably Priced Car."

Freddie Flintoff, Chris Harris and Paddy McGuinness head to the searing heat of Ethiopia in their first cars; back at the track, Chris puts the Ferrari 488 Pista and McLaren 600LT through their paces.
Freddie tries to bungee-jump a car off a dam; Paddy sets out to prove an old hearse is the ultimate family car; Chris remembers the Lotus 79 race car.

In an electric car special, Chris, Freddie and Paddy each attempt to build their own-battery powered sports car on a budget; Chris tests the Tesla Model 3 on track; Danny Boyle and Himesh Patel are the guest stars.

Chris, Freddie and Paddy set out to turn an old hearse into the ultimate family car; Chris gets to grips with the lightweight Dallara Stradale; Zara and Mike Tindall go head-to-head in the Reasonably Fast Car.

Paddy and Freddie head to Borneo for a jungle adventure with the Gurkhas, in a pair of very rare, very cheap old cars: Chris Harris tries out the world's most luxurious SUV, the Rolls-Royce Cullinan; Bob Mortimer is the studio guest.

Freddie Flintoff heads to Iceland to compete in the world's maddest motorsport; Paddy McGuinness tries out a Toyota Supra; Chris Harris investigates the story of the Lotus 79, the most beautiful F1 car of all time.
Paddy McGuinness builds his own luxurious off-roader in the shape of the Dirty Rascal; Chris samples the Rolls-Royce Cullinan.
Paddy, Freddie and Chris go on a British summer holiday in super-cheap, second-hand convertibles; Chris tests the new Ariel Atom on track, and Freddie attempts to bungee-jump an old Rover off a dam.

Paddy reveals his ultimate cheap, luxurious off-roader: the home-built "Dirty Rascal;" Chris races the £2.5m McLaren Speedtail against the RAF's newest fighter jet; Romesh Ranganathan is the studio guest.
Paddy, Freddie and Chris are sent on a high-altitude mountain expedition across Peru in second-hand American cars; Chris tests out the latest electric car from Porsche.
Jeremy Clarkson, Richard Hammond and James May buy old British roadsters from Jensen-Healey, Lotus and TVR.
The trio travels to America; comparing the Mercedes SLS, the Porsche 911 GT3 RS and the Ferrari 458 Italia.
The boys set out to boost the British economy on a trade mission to India.
Jeremy, Richard and James take a road trip across the Middle East to follow the path of the Three Wise Men.
Jeremy, Richard and James face their Australian Top Gear counterparts, and it's an all-out grudge match that will almost certainly end in tears.
Testing the Rolls-Royce Ghost, Bentley Mulsanne and Mercedes S65 AMG in Albania; trio of high-powered hatchbacks.
Discover some unusual pitfalls to look out for when buying a used car; Simon Pegg and Nick Frost are the Stars in a Reasonably Priced Car.

Freddie and Chris tackle the toughest off-road race on the planet: the brutal Baja 1000; out on track, there's a showdown between a Renault hot hatch, a Porsche sports car and an old Lamborghini; Laurence and Emilia Fox are studio guests.

Paddy, Freddie and Chris take the latest sports cars from Ferrari, Aston and Porsche on a Yorkshire road trip; on track, Chris tests out Volkswagen's fearsome ID-R electric race; YouTube sensation KSI is studio guest.

Paddy, Freddie and Chris find out if fire, police or ambulance is the fastest of the emergency services; Chris celebrates legendary rally driver Colin McRae; Paddy tests the new BMW M8; Tom Allen is the studio guest.
Testing the Tesla Model 3, Volvo S60 and BMW 3-Series by spending 24 hours in them; Chris heads to Italy to test the Ferrari SF90.
The presenters are ordered to make their cars road legal, and report to a monstrous Wall of Death; the presenters each choose a 200mph legend for a trip.
The cheapest rental cars in Europe are on the island of Cyprus; for just 30 Euros, the crew embark on a series of destructive challenges.
Injured on the trail, Jess is found by an old friend who has been rustling cattle in the area, and finds himself mistaken for one of the rustlers.
Shooters from miles around gather in Laramie for the annual Sunday Shoot, but when some disagree with the outcome, Slim and Jess step in.
Outlaws who rob and then kill a wealthy rancher find their escape is slowed when their booty -- weighty gold coins -- becomes difficult to transport.
Some women suffragettes arrive in Laramie, and Daisy invites two of them to dinner at the ranch, though Slim and the leader of the group don't see eye to eye.
When a young woman dies at the ranch, Jess escorts her son to his father, unaware that the mother wanted the boy to go to her sister in Denver.
When $50,000 goes missing from a stagecoach, and with few leads to go on, Jim suspects a safe-cracking marshal of the theft.

Hardie is transporting a prisoner to stand trial in Santa Fe, but when they stop in a small town along the way, he discovers that there's a price on the man's head -- and the mayor and sheriff may not let him leave alive.
A stolen stagecoach is found by Hardie in a town near the Mexico border, miles from any Wells Fargo station.
The murder of a casino manager.
A vengeful woman informs Hardie of a plot to rob a Wells Fargo station.
Hardie and an old friend track down a suspect who might know the location of Jefferson Davis' buried treasure.
Jim learns that his friend's fiancée holds the key to finding a stagecoach bandit.
An outlaw poses as an Army major.
Hardie wonders why a prisoner acts unconcerned about his coming murder trial.
Hardie sets out to capture gunrunners.
An Army captain wanted for desertion.
An actor visits a ghost town where he last appeared with his late wife.
Hardie faces opposition when he tries to investigate a friend's drowning death.
A Wells Fargo employee has been killed and Hardie suspects a boxer.
An incoming stage has problems with a drunken, violent passenger who turns out to be the boxer John L. Sullivan.
Hardie becomes involved with a female Wells Fargo agent.
Hardie gets assigned to protect a diamond salesman carrying a small fortune in gems.
Flint happens to learn the whereabouts of a man he's been hunting for years to kill.
Duke's resemblance to gambler Jason Carter makes him the target for a murderer's bullet.
Bill and Charlie help an old friend, John Turnbull, defend his reservation against local land sharks who look to initiate a range war.
Duke takes a job as a deputy under Hiram Winthrop, a man who wants to teach farming to the Apache.
Upon reaching Sacramento, a young wagon man falls in love with an upper society lady from the train.
When the preceding wagon train falls victim to attack, fear that their train will be next results in a mutiny among wagonmaster Chris' team.
Caroline Casteel, captured many years ago by Indians, is traded back to a man who brings her to join the wagon train.
Charlie offers support to a new woman who joined the train after being kicked out of Beaver City under suspicion of staging cons.
Wealthy merchant Martin Gatsby, a man with little compassion for the less able, wants the wagon train to keep rolling and demands that Hale leave an inexperienced rider behind.
John Augustus wins a game of cards with a Chinese merchant; his prize turns out to be a beautiful Chinese girl, which the rest of the train takes issue with.
In the midst of a dry spell and desperately in need of water, the wagon train stops at the only source of water for miles, but the owner demands an outrageous price.
A Native American tribe prepares to execute Bill, believing he tried to rob a grave site, but plans change when the chief's daughter falls in love with Bill.
The son of a wealthy rancher is severely injured in a wagon accident while his father is away, and upon his return, the father is furious about the medical care given.
Jess fills in for the sheriff, hoping for a quiet weekend, but a bank robbery in Casper leads to issues in Laramie.
When he's attacked, Jess returns fire but winds up shooting the man in the back in the scuffle, prompting the man's brothers to come to Laramie seeking revenge.
A man searching for his runaway daughter stops at the Sherman ranch, where he learns that she's a saloon girl involved with outlaws who have targeted the stage line.
Trouble follows when Jess runs into an old friend who tries to convince Jess to join his outlaw gang.
Pearl Harvey's heavily insured dog disappears when she comes to town to entertain the miners.
Hardie suspects murder when a Fargo agent allegedly commits suicide.
Outlaw plots to rob the stage from Yuma.
Hardie helps with a stolen doll.
Hardie tracks down loot from a robbery.
Kitty Thorpe wants Hardie to protect her from her escaped convict husband.
A husband searches desperately for his wife in a neighborhood where numerous murders have been committed.
A shoplifter (Coleen Gray) is blackmailed into helping the store manager (Richard Long) in a crime of his own.
A meek clerk (Dick York) plots with his associates to rob their investment firm. With Wendell Holmes.
A wanted man (Jack Carson) disappears while visiting a little-known tourist attraction in Italy. With Christopher Dark.
A recently-divorced man (Robert Webber) makes a deal with a friend (Jeremy Slate) to avoid having to pay alimony.
A man (Wayne Rogers) decides to demonstrate to his new-found girlfriend (Anne Helm) how he gets his kicks. With Brian Hutton.
A housekeeper make arrangements to keep her lover all to herself when he expresses interest in another woman.
A woman (Linda Purl) is attacked in her home and her husband (David Clennon) takes the law into his own hands.
Two retired insurance salesmen (Robert H. Harris, John Qualen) expect murder when the temperature reaches 92 degrees.
A young man (John Forsythe) returns home after an absence of four years to investigate his father's death.
A woman (Ellen Corby) tries to prevent a shootout between two gunslingers (Darren McGavin, Gene Barry).
A determined detective (Robert Emhardt) uncovers a man's scheme to have his "missing" wife declared legally dead.
A woman (Patricia Hitchcock) visiting Paris returns to her hotel room to find her ailing mother missing.
A gangster (Gene Barry) plans to punish the woman (Nancy Gates) he feels is responsible for his brother's death.
A businessman, injured in a car crash and believed by everyone to be dead, fights to signal he is alive.
A man (Everett Sloane) suspects his cook (Beulah Bondi) of being an arsenic-poisoning murderer. With Janet Ward.
A down-on-his-luck man responds to a newspaper ad from a man seeking a companion for a cross-country trip.
A man (Tom Ewell) believes an exact double is gradually taking over his life.
A woman (Judith Evelyn) is suspected of murdering her husband, who has been having an affair with another woman. With Joe Mantell and Kathleen McGuire.
A larcenous store Santa (Barry Fitzgerald) helps change the ways of a potential delinquent (Bobby Clark).
A man (Darren McGavin) tries to trick an elderly woman (Patricia Collinge) out of a family heirloom.
A man (John Qualen) is surprised to learn that the boss he thought he had murdered is still alive. With Philip Reed.
A gunman (George Mathews), intent on murdering his girlfriend, purchases an alibi.
An escaped convict (John Cassavetes) takes refuge in a farmhouse occupied by a young housewife (Marisa Pavan).
A year after the murders, a newspaper reporter (Joan Lorring) attempts to interview Lizzie Borden (Carmen Mathews) and her sister about the killings.
A bum (Robert Newton) witnesses a murder and decide to take advantage of the situation. With Philip Reed.
A police detective (Charles Bronson) investigating a murder focuses on a strange ventriloquist (Claude Rains).
A female reporter (Claire Trevor) encounters problem trying to leave Eastern Europe after meeting a soccer star.
A man (Mark Damon) arrives at a monastery bent on revenge and is convinced by a kind priest (Everett Sloane) to mend his heart.
An English man (John Williams) murders his wife and moves to California, thinking he has committed the perfect crime.
Two greedy brothers plan to murder their elderly aunt (Mildred Natwick) in an attempt to inherit her money.
A desperate couple (Charles Bronson, Norma Crane) plans to rob an eccentric old woman (Estelle Winwood).
An angel (Alan Napier) allows a murdered mystery writer (John Williams) to return to Earth to uncover his killer.
An unemployed man (John Qualen) needing money is hired by an unknown employer (Lorne Greene) to commit murder.
A man (Philip Abbott) is startled to see a portrait of his first wife four years after she disappeared.
An antiques dealer (Robert H. Harris) decides his art objects are too beautiful to sell. With Louise Larabee.
An insecure woman (Phyllis Thaxter) who can't control her drinking loses control at a cocktail party.
Professional killers (Jack Cassidy, Harry Townes) with the same employer find that each has the other as his next target.
